items.description:
## Summary

A destination path supplied to virtualenv can be interpreted as shell syntax by a generated POSIX console launcher. The
app-data seeder and pip delegate launcher generation to distlib but supply the interpreter path in a form that does not
preserve it as literal data in the shell wrapper.

POSIX console scripts generated by the app-data seeder or pip when the interpreter path requires a shell wrapper.
Windows executable launchers are not affected by this path.

An attacker must influence the environment destination passed to virtualenv, and the user must subsequently run a
generated launcher. The attacker does not need to modify an installed executable or control the user's app-data cache.

items.title: Pillow: MSP RLE decoder expands a tiny file into unbounded memory
items.description:
### Summary
The MSP RLE decoder expands run-length data into an in-memory buffer with no cap tied to the declared image size. A small file that passes the pixel-count check can force hundreds of megabytes or more of allocation when the application loads pixels.

### Details
The MSP decoder writes each run into an unbounded `io.BytesIO` and can expand roughly 85x per run:

- `src/PIL/MspImagePlugin.py:144-146`

### Impact
Memory-exhaustion denial of service from a tiny crafted image in any application that loads pixels. The expansion is decoupled from the declared pixel count, so `MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` does not bound it.

## Summary

The path traversal fix released for [GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/security/advisories/GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9) can be bypassed on Windows by using a backslash in the redirect URL pathname.

The fixed code joins an attacker-controlled URL pathname with the Vite root using `node:path/posix`, then passes that string to Vite's file allowlist check. items.description:
## Summary

When a user exports content through `@apostrophecms/import-export`, the module copies the generated archive into uploadfs at `/exports/` and returns a public URL under `/uploads/exports/`. The filename is fully deterministic: site `shortName`, document type, a `YYYYMMDDHHmmss` timestamp, and the format extension. There is no secret token.

Don't add `allow="hid"` / `allow="usb"` to untrusted iframes, or make the decision in your `select-hid-device` / `select-usb-device` handler using `details.frame`.

items.description:
### Summary

An attacker sending an absolute-form request can spoof the scheme used.

### Impact

If user code depends on the `Request.scheme` attribute for anything security related, an attacker may be able to circumvent this logic, tricking the application into thinking a connection is encrypted when it is not, or vice versa.

### Workaround

A WAF rule to reject absolute-form requests (legitimate requests should only use this form for proxies).

items.description:
### Summary

A subdomain can remove the Host-Only flag from an existing cookie to a parent domain.

### Impact

A user accessing untrusted subdomains could see their Host-Only protections stripped from cookies. Given most usecases won't reflect these cookies to a browser, the impact is limited.

items.title: AIOHTTP: Connector pool exhaustion via Max-Age overflow
items.description:
### Summary

An overflow in Max-Age processing can skip closing a connection.

### Impact

An attacker may be able to exhaust the connection pool temporarily, until garbage collection resolves the connections.

items.title: AIOHTTP: Pure-Python parser request smuggling

The pure Python parser is vulnerable to an HTTP request smuggling attack.

### Impact

If users are using the Python parser (`AIOHTTP_NO_EXTENSIONS`, or not a standard wheel installed), then an application may be vulnerable to a request smuggling attack.

### Workaround

Switch to the default C parser.

items.description:

items.title: certifi bundles emSign root CAs with compromised intermediate CA keys

Certifi versions before 2026.10.18 include the `emSign ECC Root CA - G3` root certificate in their bundled CA store. Eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates that chain to this root have compromised private keys and the CA has revoked them.

If the attacker is also on-path, they can intercept or modify TLS traffic from clients that trust the certifi bundle. Examples include `requests`, `urllib3` and `pip`, and the Python.org macOS installer.
